summary: The module fingerprints /v1/agent/self, falls back to /v1/status/leader for ACL-strict hosts, and touches /v1/catalog/services, /v1/catalog/nodes, /v1/kv/?recurse — but only counts nodes/keys and never extracts the actual data or attempts any active escalation. It ignores the biggest single-request win (POST /v1/acl/bootstrap), never tests KV writability, discards node/service addresses that other recce modules would consume, and although `analyze(creds=...)` accepts credentials, no code path ever sends X-Consul-Token. It also does not touch the Consul RPC/DNS/Serf side-ports (8300/8301/8302/8600).
existing_capabilities: HTTP with transparent HTTPS/TLS retry (unverified ctx)

missing_capabilities.name: ACL bootstrap escalation (PUT /v1/acl/bootstrap)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Consul ACL HTTP API — Bootstrap ACLs (developer.hashicorp.com/consul/api-docs/acl#bootstrap-acls). Endpoint returns 200 with a full-privilege management SecretID if the cluster has never been bootstrapped; 403 with 'ACL bootstrap no longer allowed' otherwise.
missing_capabilities.description: Single PUT to /v1/acl/bootstrap on any ACL-not-yet-bootstrapped cluster returns a permanent management token = cluster-admin. Module never attempts it. Only safe active probe of comparable value in the entire module surface.

missing_capabilities.name: KV value extraction (not just key count)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Consul KV HTTP API (/v1/kv/<key>?recurse) — response contains base64-encoded Value field. developer.hashicorp.com/consul/api-docs/kv
missing_capabilities.description: Docstring promises 'credentials, feature flags, service configs' but code only counts entries. Need to (a) base64-decode Value, (b) flag keys matching password|token|secret|api_key|aws|gcp|vault|jwt|priv, (c) surface top-N as evidence in the finding. This is the money endpoint and its actual money is thrown away.

missing_capabilities.name: KV write-access test (PUT /v1/kv/<probe>)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Consul KV HTTP API — Create/Update Key. Write access under default-allow ACL enables RCE against any host running consul-template, envconsul, nomad, or vault-agent that renders KV values into config/scripts.
missing_capabilities.description: Write into KV is a documented RCE primitive on any subscriber using consul-template/envconsul. Module never probes writability. Even a HEAD/OPTIONS + a scoped PUT+DELETE of /v1/kv/recce-probe/<rand> would confirm.

missing_capabilities.name: Snapshot endpoint (GET /v1/snapshot)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Consul Snapshot HTTP API — developer.hashicorp.com/consul/api-docs/snapshot. Returns a gzipped tarball of the entire cluster state (KV, ACL tokens, sessions, catalog, intentions, prepared queries).
missing_capabilities.description: One request pulls the complete Raft state including token SecretIDs. Requires management-level access normally but often exposed on default-allow deployments. Not probed.

missing_capabilities.name: Credentialed path — accepts creds but never sends X-Consul-Token
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Consul HTTP API auth — X-Consul-Token header (developer.hashicorp.com/consul/api-docs/api-structure). Also Authorization: Bearer <token> since 1.11.
missing_capabilities.description: analyze(creds=...) signature accepts credentials, drops them on the floor. _http() has no token param. Any Consul token looted from KV of another host, git, Vault, or env leaks cannot be replayed. Blocks the entire credentialed runbook that neighbouring modules populate.

missing_capabilities.name: Per-service address enumeration (/v1/catalog/service/<name>)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Consul Catalog HTTP API — List Nodes for Service. Response items contain ServiceAddress, ServicePort, Address (node IP), TaggedAddresses (lan/wan), NodeMeta.
missing_capabilities.description: Module returns only the service NAME map. The per-service call yields Address:Port of every instance = complete internal service graph (postgres backends, redis, vault, nomad, mesh sidecars). This is the primary lateral-movement payoff of an unauth Consul.

missing_capabilities.name: Full node inventory (/v1/agent/members and /v1/catalog/nodes payload)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Consul Agent HTTP API — List Members (Serf gossip view: Name, Addr, Port, Tags, Status, ProtocolCur, dc, role). /v1/catalog/nodes returns Address + TaggedAddresses per node.
missing_capabilities.description: Currently only len(nodes) is retained. Names, IPv4/IPv6 tagged addresses, dc/role tags, and Serf gossip status are all discarded — losing every pivot target and every WAN federation link.

missing_capabilities.name: Cross-service wire — publish discovered services/hosts to the pipeline
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Internal recce discovery pipeline; Consul catalog surfaces vault/nomad/postgres/mysql/redis/rabbitmq/kafka as named services with addresses.
missing_capabilities.description: Findings/analyze return services + kv info but do not feed them back as Host/Port additions or as hints to service-specific modules (vault, redis, postgres, nomad). Consul is the single richest cross-service oracle in the environment and its output currently dead-ends in a text finding.

missing_capabilities.name: Agent/self extraction loss (datacenter, encryption, TLS floor, role, telemetry, Raft protocol)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Consul Agent HTTP API — Read Configuration (/v1/agent/self). Fields include Config.Datacenter, Config.NodeID, Config.Server, DebugConfig.EncryptKey (redacted flag), DebugConfig.TLSMinVersion, DebugConfig.RaftProtocol, DebugConfig.Ports, Telemetry.*, Meta.
missing_capabilities.description: The response is parsed once for Version+ACL only. Missing: datacenter federation name (cross-DC pivot), Server bool (targeting servers vs agents), gossip encryption presence (unencrypted gossip = MitM), TLSMinVersion (TLS1.0/1.1 findings), Ports map (Serf/RPC/DNS overrides), Telemetry endpoints (Prometheus/StatsD leakage), NodeID (cluster-unique pivot key).

missing_capabilities.name: Raft cluster topology (/v1/operator/raft/configuration)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Consul Operator HTTP API — Read Raft Configuration. Returns Servers[] with ID, Node, Address, Leader, Voter.
missing_capabilities.description: Reveals every Consul server IP and voter status = direct list of highest-value targets (compromising any voter = quorum influence). Not touched.

missing_capabilities.name: Service-mesh intentions and Connect CA (/v1/connect/intentions, /v1/connect/ca/roots)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Consul Connect HTTP API — Intentions list (SourceName -> DestinationName Action=allow|deny) and CA Roots (PEM cert bundle for mTLS).
missing_capabilities.description: Intentions = the machine-readable trust map of the mesh; picks lateral targets for you. CA roots expose the mTLS PKI (issuer, expiry, key algorithm) and confirm whether Connect is in use.

missing_capabilities.name: Consul DNS side-port (53-compatible on 8600/udp+tcp)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Consul DNS Interface — <service>.service.<dc>.consul, <node>.node.consul, SRV records with instance ports (developer.hashicorp.com/consul/docs/services/discovery/dns-overview).
missing_capabilities.description: is_consul() only recognises 8500/8501. 8600 is a separate always-anonymous service-enumeration channel — DNS SRV over UDP works even when the HTTP API is ACL-locked. No probe, no fingerprint.

missing_capabilities.name: Serf gossip encryption detection (8301/8302)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Serf LAN (8301) and WAN (8302); Consul gossip encryption governed by encrypt config (16/24/32-byte base64 key). Absence of EncryptKey in agent/self = cleartext gossip on the wire.
missing_capabilities.description: No detection of Serf ports or unencrypted-gossip condition, which enables cluster join spoofing and passive membership sniff.

missing_capabilities.name: Anonymous token privilege enumeration (/v1/acl/token/self, /v1/acl/policies)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Consul ACL HTTP API — Read Self Token, List Policies. Anonymous token shows Rules/Policies attached to the empty SecretID.
missing_capabilities.description: Confirms *exactly* what the anon token is allowed to do (e.g., 'operator = write' on a mis-scoped policy would upgrade the finding). Also lists all policy names = leaks role model.

missing_capabilities.name: Version -> CVE mapping
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Consul security advisories: CVE-2020-7955 (RPC), CVE-2020-13250, CVE-2021-32574 (script injection via consul-template rendering), CVE-2022-24687 (SAML DoS), CVE-2022-40716 (SAML auth bypass, Enterprise), CVE-2020-28053 (HTTP request smuggling for ACL bypass <1.9.5).
missing_capabilities.description: Version is captured but never scored against known Consul CVEs — most notably CVE-2020-28053 (ACL bypass on <1.9.5 flips the whole ACL-enforcing branch into unauth).

missing_capabilities.name: Session and prepared-query enumeration (/v1/session/list, /v1/query)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Consul Session and Prepared Query HTTP APIs. Sessions bind KV locks; prepared queries embed service templates and often DC failover chains.
missing_capabilities.description: Session hijack + KV lock steal is a documented Consul primitive; prepared queries reveal cross-DC service failover targets. Neither surface probed.

missing_capabilities.name: Catalog registration abuse (PUT /v1/catalog/register, PUT /v1/agent/service/register)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Consul Catalog / Agent HTTP APIs — Register Entity / Register Service. Under default-allow, arbitrary services can be inserted into DNS + catalog, redirecting mesh consumers.
missing_capabilities.description: Not tested. Complements the KV-write test: catalog write = service impersonation / DNS poisoning within the mesh.

missing_capabilities.name: Legacy ACL surface (Consul <1.4 endpoints /v1/acl/list, /v1/acl/info)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Consul legacy ACL system pre-1.4 (developer.hashicorp.com/consul/docs/security/acl/acl-legacy). Different endpoint set; still deployed on long-lived clusters.
missing_capabilities.description: Version-gated fallback to legacy /v1/acl/list is not present. On <1.4 clusters current probe misses the ACL model entirely.

missing_capabilities.name: Consul RPC side-port 8300
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Consul server RPC on 8300/tcp (MessagePack over TLS or plaintext). Peer/join port for federation.
missing_capabilities.description: 8300 is not fingerprinted; identifying servers vs agents on the wire has value for target selection even without an RPC-client implementation.

cross_service_wire_gaps: Discovered services in /v1/catalog/services (e.g. 'vault','nomad','postgres','redis','mysql','rabbitmq','kafka','elasticsearch') are never re-emitted as hints/targets to their respective recce service modules.

Per-service Address:Port from /v1/catalog/service/<name> is never emitted as newly-discovered Host/Port entries into the pipeline (would materially expand the scan surface with zero extra network reach).
Node IPs and TaggedAddresses from /v1/catalog/nodes + /v1/agent/members are collapsed to a count; they should feed Host discovery.

KV values (once decoded) matching Vault paths (secret/, kv/), DB URIs (postgres://, mysql://, redis://), cloud creds (AKIA, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, SAS tokens), and SSH keys are never surfaced as credentials into the shared creds bag other modules consume.
Connect CA root PEM is never surfaced to the TLS/PKI finding stream (issuer, expiry, weak-key checks).

Consul-issued tokens (from bootstrap or KV leakage) are never registered as replayable creds for the credentialed runbook, nor pushed into other services that trust Consul-derived auth (Vault Consul auth backend, Nomad).
Datacenter/federation name from agent/self is not published as a scope tag, so cross-DC catalog queries (?dc=<other>) that would reveal WAN peers are never issued.
priority_gaps: 1. POST /v1/acl/bootstrap — one-request cluster admin escalation on un-bootstrapped clusters (critical)
2. Extract & classify KV VALUES (base64-decode, secret-key regex), not just count keys — the docstring's promise is currently a lie (critical)
3. KV write-access test — direct RCE primitive against consul-template/envconsul/nomad consumers (critical)
4. GET /v1/snapshot — full cluster state dump including token SecretIDs (critical)
5. Send X-Consul-Token — plumb the analyze(creds=) argument that is currently ignored (high)
7. Feed discovered services + node addresses back into recce discovery/creds pipelines (high, cross-service wire)
8. Rich /v1/agent/self extraction: datacenter, Server bool, EncryptKey presence, TLSMinVersion, RaftProtocol, Ports, Telemetry (high)
11. Consul DNS port 8600 recognition + SRV service enumeration (medium)
12. Version->CVE mapping (esp. CVE-2020-28053 pre-1.9.5 ACL bypass) (medium)
notes: Airgap constraint respected in recommendations — all listed probes are pure stdlib http.client/socket work. The module already has svcprobe/budget/progress plumbing to add these cheaply. No implementation performed. Also note that _http()'s TLS retry re-issues the same request on every SSLError — worth flagging separately, but per instructions cosmetic tweaks are excluded.
